newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-JAYASURIYA MISSES RECORD, SRI LANKA PILE UP RUNS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-JAYASURIYA MISSES RECORD, SRI LANKA PILE UP RUNS.

text.p: Sanath Jayasuriya missed out on Brian Lara's world record test score of 375 as Sri Lanka took their first innings score to 738 for three at lunch on the final day of the first test against India on Wednesday.
Jayasuriya, 326 not out overnight, was caught by Saurav Ganguly off Rajesh Chauhan in the fourth over of the day for 340.
Jayasuriya's dismissal followed that of his longstanding partner Roshan Mahanama for 225 in the previous over. The pair put on 576 -- a record for any wicket in test cricket.
Despite the early dismissals of their two tormentors, the Indian bowlers enjoyed little respite as Aravinda de Silva and skipper Arjuna Ranatunga continued to plunder runs at will.
The fourth wicket pair shared an entertaining stand of 123 up to the interval.
De Silva was unbeaten on 53, having hit nine fours, and Ranatunga's 65 included 11 fours.
The left-handed Jayasuriya began confidently by hitting three fours. He added two further singles before offering a tired stroke to Ganguly at silly point.
Jayasuriya's anguish was evident as he hit the ground with his bat. A packed stadium rose to applaud him all the way back to the pavilion.
Jayasuriya's marathon 578-ball innings lasted 799 minutes and included 36 fours and two sixes. It was the fourth highest innings in tests, after Lara's 375, Garry Sobers' 365 and Len Hutton's 364.
Mahanama fell leg before to leg spinner Anil Kumble. He batted for 753 minutes, faced 561 balls and hit 28 fours.
Security personnel manning the stadium were unable to control spectators scaling high iron gates surrounding the ground as they struggled to see Jayasuriya's attempt on Lara's record.
Baton-wielding police were forced to charge sections of the crowd to restore order.
